title: The False and True Riders
english: Having confidence in themselves, they will line up against those against whom they have the fight and the war, as each one might say thankfully: 'The Lord is my light and my savior; whom shall I fear? (Ps 27:1) The Lord is the defender of my life; from whom shall I shrink in cowardice? (Ps 27:2) In the approaching of those who do evil to eat my flesh, those who afflict me, and my enemies themselves have grown weak and fallen; (Ps 27:3) if an encampment is lined up against me, my heart shall not fear; (Ps 27:3) if a war rises up against me, in this I hope.' (Ps 27:5).

Having the same courage, he who sings the third Psalm also was emboldened to say: 'I will not fear from ten thousands of people surrounding me.' (Ps 3:6). To those thus arrayed, the word, encouraging them, says: 'One of you shall pursue a thousand, and two shall put ten thousand to flight' (Lk 10:19), not of men alone as warriors, but also of the invisible.

To those having the struggle, those fighting for Christ and having clothed themselves in His good fortune say: 'Our struggle is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers and powers and the cosmic dictators of this darkness and the spiritual things of wickedness.' (Eph 6:12). For, having been surrounded by all these warriors, he who, by the designation of God, is like an unassailable shield, trembling with courage, says: 'Encompassing, they have surrounded me, and by the name of the Lord I defended myself against them.' (Ps 18:4). The same thing this one also cries out triumphantly: 'Behold, the Lord helps me; who shall harm me?' (Ps 27:7).

And the riders of horses shall be put to shame. (Zech 10:5) And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will let them dwell, for I have loved them, and in no way will I turn them away, because I am the Lord their God, and I will listen to them. (Zech 10:6) And they shall be as warriors of Ephraim, and their heart shall rejoice as if in wine; and their children shall be seen and shall be glad, and their heart shall rejoice in the Lord. (Zech 10:7)
Those greatly trusting in a cavalry line, when the requirements of war arise from a purpose, [are] shame...

They are being deceived, having learned through experience that 'a false horse is for salvation.' Concerning those fighting in this way, the choir of the saints says: 'These are in chariots and these are on horses, but we shall rejoice in the name of the Lord; they themselves were overthrown and fell, but we have risen and been set upright' (Ps 20:6). Similarly to these, the tyrant of Egypt and all those marshaled with him were dejected when they were crushed in the Red Sea, as a victory hymn began to be sung against them from: 'I will sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously honored; he has thrown horse and rider into the sea' (Ex 15:1). Concerning these riders, it is also said in one of the Psalms: 'From your rebuke, O God of Jacob, those standing on horses have been unseated' (Ps 68:17).

Who, then, are these who are being overseen? If horses are understood to be human bodies, because they are skittish and unruly, souls are found to be riders who are not disciplined, not skillfully subduing the horses upon which they ride; therefore they also endure shame, being tossed about, as the prophetic word says: 'The riders of horses shall be put to shame' (Ps 68:25). According to another understanding, the pompous and sophistical men were understood to be horses, upon whom evil powers ride in a disorderly manner, not knowing how to guide with reins but being carried by a disorderly force, who, because they approach the four-footed passions unskillfully, shall be put to shame; they fall into pits because they doze and slumber, not enduring the things of those who ride salvationally. For the soul that subdues and leads the body surrounding it is not a mere passenger, nor a rider, but a horseman, skillfully controlling the hooves.

Likewise, certain divine powers, riding with equestrian skill, are carried among the best of men, being carried by the force of divine teaching, having as leader and first-fruit the one whose horsemanship is salvation, concerning whom it is said: 'Mount upon your horses and your horsemanship...'
